newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Slightly higher NZ inflation seen - NZIER consensus.
newsitem.headline: Slightly higher NZ inflation seen - NZIER consensus.

text.p: Respondents to a consensus survey in December see higher New Zealand inflation in 1997-98 and 1998-99 and a higher exchange rate than they did in September, the New Zealand Institute of Economic Research said on Friday.
Respondents still see 1.8 percent GDP growth in the year to March 1997, but have trimmed their 1997-98 growth estimate to 3.0 percent from 3.2 percent.
Ninety-day bank bill rates are seen at an average 8.9 percent in the March 1997 year and 7.8 percent the year after, versus 9.4 percent and 8.3 percent seen previously.
The New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index is seen averaging 66.0 in the year to March 1997 and at 66.0 and 66.6 in the following two years.

The consensus forecasts reflect last month's announcement of a centre-right coalition between the National and New Zealand First parties, which agreed to widen the central bank's inflation target to 0-3 percent from 0-2 percent.
As a result, respondents now see 1.3 percent inflation in the March 1998 year, up from a previous consensus forecast of 1.0 percent.
The consensus forecast unemployment is slightly higher, compared to September. The jobless rate is forecast to stay at 6.7 percent for 1997 and 1998, falling to 6.5 percent in 1999.
NZIER said the outlook for the balance of payments was for a continued deterioration, to deficits of NZ$4.1 billion and $4.4 billion in 1997-98 and 1998-99.
The consensus forecasts are drawn from 12 respondents including the Reserve Bank and Treasury.
